slides.title: Former Li Auto AI Chief Scientist Chen Wei Raises Funds for Embodied AI Home Robot Startup
slides.tldr: FUNDING FOR EMBODIED AI HOME ROBOTS
slides.highlight: Chen Wei has raised funds for an embodied AI startup focused on home robots, which aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: ABM-SIRTEM: A Hybrid Agent-Based and Epidemiological Model for Pandemic Response
slides.highlight: This research proposes a hybrid model integrating individual-level economic productivity and welfare with disease dynamics, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: ABM-SIRTEM is a hybrid model coupling population-level disease dynamics with agent-based socioeconomic behavior and compliance.
card.key_idea: It integrates SIRTEM epidemiological compartments with an ABM where agents update compliance based on welfare (economic productivity, mental well-being, and health risk) using evolutionary game theory.
card.evaluation: Calibrated using Bayesian optimization against historical COVID-19 positive/negative test counts from four U.S. states; results broadly reproduce major wave timings.
card.limitation: Evaluations assess calibration fit rather than predictive performance on held-out data; negative test count fits vary across states.

slides.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark to evaluate whether dialogue systems can distinguish between interruptions and backchannels based on context, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ECHO is a diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex dialogue to evaluate context-sensitive turn-taking decisions.
card.key_idea: It uses matched-contrast pairs where the same user insertion is paired with different dialogue contexts to distinguish between interruptions (Yield) and backchannels/off-talk (Keep).
card.evaluation: Evaluated four speech systems and Gemini (text reference) using Pairwise Action Success Rate (PASR). Results show most systems have a strong Yield bias.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized audio rather than natural speech, and interruption waveforms include label-dependent RMS scaling and onset emphasis.

slides.title: Audio-Visual Turn-taking Prediction in Cocktail Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This research evaluates audio-visual predictive turn-taking models in noisy cocktail-party scenarios, providing insights into modality-specific degradation and adaptation. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in complex human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Audio-visual turn-taking models degrade in cocktail-party scenarios but improve via large-scale pre-training and fine-tuning.
card.key_idea: Evaluates Voice Activity Projection (VAP) variants (Audio, Video, Multimodal) on AVCocktail, analyzing how domain shift and pre-training scale affect generalisation and adaptation to noisy environments.
card.evaluation: Tested on Candor and AVCocktail datasets using weighted F1 scores; results show MM-VAP is most robust, with up to 30% relative improvement after fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Models suffer from catastrophic forgetting of clean domains after fine-tuning and rely on suboptimal high-level OpenFace visual features.

slides.title: Gaze as Evidence for Common Grounding: A Cross-Corpus Analysis of MapTask and MUNDEX
slides.tldr: GAZE AS A CUE FOR COMMON GROUNDING
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how gaze features, such as gaze entropy and transitions, correlate with grounding and reference interpretation in collaborative tasks. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Gaze patterns consistently signal grounding across different collaborative tasks, most notably for the task leader.
card.key_idea: Mapping MapTask and MUNDEX gaze ontologies to a shared partner/task/away vocabulary to analyze associations between gaze features and grounding states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Mann-Whitney U tests and logistic regression on MapTask and MUNDEX; modest macro-F1 improvements over controls using grouped cross-validation.
card.limitation: Small effect sizes, limited participant counts, and sensitivity to the unit of inference (dialogue vs. participant) limit generalization.

slides.title: Online Multimodal Workload Assessment in Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a transparent framework for online workload assessment in contact-rich physical human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: An interpretable multimodal framework for online interaction workload assessment in contact-rich physical human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Integrates interaction wrench, TCP kinematics, and skin conductance into four interpretable factors, using path curvature and task progression for context-adaptive weighting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 24 participants across 18 environmental conditions; used leave-one-subject-out validation against pupillometry and learning baselines (MLP, TCN, LSTM).
card.limitation: Correspondence with the physiological reference is weak near task onset (ρ_early = 0.002).

slides.title: DiaWhisper-DPO: Role-Attributed Transcription of Clinical Interviews via Failure-Mined Preference Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces DiaWhisper-DPO, an end-to-end model for transcription and role attribution that reduces errors compared to cascaded systems. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and identity recognition within human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: DiaWhisper-DPO enables end-to-end role-attributed clinical transcription using failure-mined preference optimization to reduce decoding errors.
card.key_idea: LoRA-tuned Whisper-large-v3 with an auxiliary role head, refined via DPO using genuine decoding failures as rejected completions and ground truth as chosen completions.
card.evaluation: Tested on DAIC-WOZ and PDCH-HAMD against cascaded baselines; achieved 0.973 role accuracy and 0.119 DER on DAIC-WOZ, showing significant seed stability.
card.limitation: DAIC-WOZ evaluation relies on synthetic interviewer audio; outputs require human verification due to clinical risks of misattribution.

slides.title: Negation Beyond the Verbal Channel: Temporal Multimodal Correlates in Dialogue
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that nonverbal behaviors, particularly facial features, can predict negation cues in dialogue, supporting HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Nonverbal behavior can distinguish spoken negation cues from control words without using lexical or acoustic data.
card.key_idea: Used time-series classifiers (e.g., RocketPFN) as probes on VR-captured multimodal streams (gaze, face, body) to analyze temporal and modality-specific correlates of negation cues.
card.evaluation: 10-fold cross-validation on 27 VR interviews; compared 20 models. Strongest probes reached .75 mean AUROC; results robust across POS-matched controls.
card.limitation: Data is limited to a single VR survey setting and dominated by the German word 'nicht' (~80%).

slides.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ROBOT PREFERENCE LEARNING VIA DYNAMIC IMPLICATION MODELING
slides.highlight: This work introduces IMPLIED, a method that learns to infer and revise action labels from human feedback to improve robot behavior adaptation. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: IMPLIED improves robot preference learning by dynamically revising labels for unchosen actions based on feedback.
card.key_idea: A mixture model combining a fixed-rule prior with a Gaussian Process classifier that learns to infer and revise accepted/rejected labels for unchosen actions using direct evidence.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (sandwich-making, block-sorting) and physical pizza-making studies against fixed-rule and LLM baselines using L2 error, conflict proportion, and F1 scores.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for co-adapting a musculoskeletal human policy with an exoskeleton controller across multiple locomotor skills. It aligns with MOSAIC's focus on coadaptive loops and skill acquisition for human-AI alignment.

card.one_liner: UniExo provides a unified, multi-skill controller for exoskeletons supporting diverse locomotion activities and smooth transitions without mode switching.
card.key_idea: Distills four single-skill musculoskeletal experts into one latent-conditioned policy, then co-adapts a hip exoskeleton controller using multi-agent RL and domain randomization.
card.evaluation: Simulation tracking (94.7% success) and hardware tests with six participants across four treadmill speeds and a multi-skill route.
card.limitation: Limited to four flat-ground skills; lacks metabolic cost measurements and fully consistent muscle activation patterns compared to EMG.

slides.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
slides.tldr: DUAL-PROCESS AGENTS WITH MEMORY AND SELF-REFLECTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Self-Reflection Module for execution-time validation and an Adaptive Memory Module for episodic storage, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: Dual-process agents improve in interactive environments by combining salience-gated memory with bounded execution-time reflection.
card.key_idea: Extends SwiftSage with an Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) for episodic retrieval and a Self-Reflection Module (SRM) for action validation and stagnation-triggered corrective intervention.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ScienceWorld; full system achieved highest mean score (64.62) and success rate (43.17%), with SRM being the strongest standalone contributor.
card.limitation: Memory is primarily episodic without semantic consolidation, and SRM relies on hand-crafted stagnation thresholds and deterministic repair policies.

slides.authors: João Meneses dos Santos et al.

slides.title: Agility Unveils Humanoid Built to Work With People
slides.highlight: The unveiling of a humanoid robot designed to work with people is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Designing Against Deskilling: Metacognitive Feedback Reduces Cognitive Offloading to LLM Assistants
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that metacognitive feedback can reduce cognitive offloading to LLM assistants and improve performance, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition for effective human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive feedback reduces cognitive offloading to LLM assistants and improves subsequent unaided skill performance.
card.key_idea: Comparing metacognitive feedback (making AI-use implications explicit) and effort-based rewards (incentivizing less assistance) to prevent deskilling during fraction arithmetic practice.
card.evaluation: Preregistered online experiment (N=704) using a 2x2-plus-control design; measured answer offloading and unaided test scores. Results show metacognitive feedback was effective, while rewards were not.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: PRISM uses a transformer encoder to infer human interaction traits from passive observations, reducing collision rates in social robot navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: PRISM improves social robot navigation by passively inferring pedestrian interaction styles from observed trajectories.
card.key_idea: A transformer encoder uses Rank-N-Contrast loss to map trajectories into a continuous ordinal latent space, providing interaction-style vectors and stability scores to the policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in PyBullet simulations using ORCA pedestrians; PRISM reduced collision rates (e.g., 0.19 to 0.12) compared to the HEIGHT geometry-only baseline.
card.limitation: Results are limited to synthetic ORCA-based heterogeneity and lack confidence intervals or real-world pedestrian data validation.

slides.title: Mental Models in Human-AI Interaction: Methods and Challenges in the Generative and Agentic AI Era
slides.tldr: CRITICAL REASSESSMENT OF MENTAL MODELS IN HUMAN-AI INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This work examines how users reason about and interact with AI systems, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on modeling the state of hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: A workshop proposal to reassess mental model research in the era of generative and agentic AI.
card.key_idea: Critical reassessment of mental model conceptualization and elicitation methods to address opacity and agency in contemporary AI systems through papers, exercises, and discussions.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text describes a proposed workshop program rather than a completed empirical study.
card.limitation: Heterogeneous elicitation methods and conceptual overlap with folk theories hinder the commensurability of current human-AI interaction research.

slides.title: Beyond "ChatGPT Can Make Mistakes": Designing Interventions to Support Metacognitive Monitoring in AI-Assisted Work
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE MONITORING INTERVENTIONS FOR AI ASSISTANCE
slides.highlight: This research explores design interventions to improve users' metacognitive monitoring of AI system competence, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: A design space and experiment exploring interventions to improve user metacognitive monitoring in AI-assisted work.
card.key_idea: Proposed a design space based on time, level (whose competence is judged), and source (who supplies the cue) to organize metacognitive interventions.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects experiment (N=917) using 12 planning problems. Reliability cards and contrasting replies improved monitoring (calibration/sensitivity), but no task-performance gains were found.
card.limitation: Interventions lowered usability and increased workload; monitoring improvements did not translate to better task accuracy.

slides.authors: Manuel A. D. Santos et al.

slides.title: Affective Shared Autonomy: Temporal Affect Dynamics and Subjective Evaluation in Bimanual Teleoperation Tasks
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator affective states, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: An affect-aware shared autonomy framework that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator emotional states.
card.key_idea: A multimodal fusion model (facial video, cardiac signals, arm kinematics) estimates affective states to trigger assistance only during sustained adverse states, preserving user agency.
card.evaluation: User study (N=30) across three modes; measured state proportions and NASA-TLX. Affect-aware assistance increased productive states by 39.7% over manual control.
card.limitation: Personalized affective models require iterative calibration, causing mild unpredictability and slightly lower satisfaction in time-constrained trials.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals across four ontological levels, supporting MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic agent models for human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals via hierarchical prediction and ontological constraints.
card.key_idea: A Hierarchical Planning Decoder attached to a frozen encoder, using soft neuro-symbolic regularization and hard reachability masks to predict intentions across four ontological levels.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15,002 multimodal episodes (NTU RGB+D 120). Outperformed sequential baselines in top-5 accuracy and joint logic constraint satisfaction.
card.limitation: Challenges remain in compositional goal generalization and unordered set prediction.

slides.title: Disentangling Long-Term Memory via Latent Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
slides.highlight: LGM introduces a neuro-symbolic framework using sparse autoencoders to disentangle long-term memory in a latent space, supporting the development of LLM-based agents for MIMIC.

card.one_liner: LGM disentangles long-term user memory in a latent space to improve personalized reasoning and efficiency.
card.key_idea: Uses a sparse autoencoder for concept decomposition and a query-conditioned latent graph with relational message passing to synthesize compact memory prefix tokens for LLM conditioning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on PersonaMem, PrefEval, and PersonaMem-v2 using Qwen and Gemma backbones; outperformed SOTA baselines in accuracy, latency, and token consumption.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Sensemaking as Artifact: Accumulated Influence in AI-Mediated Information Environments
slides.highlight: This work explores how generative AI transforms private sensemaking into derivative artifacts that influence subsequent viewers' perceptions, relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: GenAI allows private sensemaking to become externalized artifacts that shape subsequent viewers' interpretations of information.
card.key_idea: The authors propose a framework for AI-mediated visual communication where source artifacts are transformed into derivative artifacts, creating a cycle of accumulated influence across information environments.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper presents a theoretical framework and research agenda rather than an empirical study with datasets.
card.limitation: The paper identifies risks like sycophancy, loss of provenance, and reduced collective diversity, but does not provide empirical solutions.

slides.title: What Counts as Strategic Reasoning? A Systematic Mapping of Chess Research on Humans, Engines, and Language Models
slides.highlight: This study identifies gaps in chess research regarding metacognition and human-AI collaboration, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: A systematic mapping of 84 chess research studies analyzing strategic reasoning across humans, engines, and LLMs.
card.key_idea: The study classifies research by agent type, strategic-reasoning stage, and evaluation dimension to identify gaps in explicit planning, explanation, and metacognition.
card.evaluation: Systematic mapping of 84 core study families (2023-2026) from Scopus, Web of Science, and Zotero using multi-label coding.
card.limitation: The mapping aggregates different hybrid architectures and does not distinguish between human augmentation and genuine human-AI synergy.

slides.title: Dynamic Generalized Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC GENERALIZED GW-OT FOR STRUCTURE-AWARE ALIGNMENT
slides.highlight: This work introduces TP-DATE, a framework for dynamic Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport that preserves spatial structure during trajectory reconstruction, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for intent alignment.

card.one_liner: TP-DATE provides a simulation-free framework for dynamic structure-aware optimal transport using travelling-pair flow matching.
card.key_idea: It generalizes Quadratic-form OT (QOT) by modeling interacting conditional paths (travelling pairs) and marginalizing their interactions into a single vector field via flow matching.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on synthetic and real spatial transcriptomics data; results show improved preservation of spatial structure and 3D dynamics reconstruction.
card.limitation: The dynamic formulation is currently restricted to cases where the source and target spaces are the same.
